landmarks.name: Laas Geel
landmarks.writeup: Ancient cave paintings dating back over 5,000 years, showcasing early African rock art.

wiki.extract: Laas Geel, also spelled Laas Gaal, are cave formations on the rural outskirts of Hargeisa, Somaliland, situated in the Maroodi Jeex region of the country. They contain some of the earliest known cave paintings of domesticated African aurochs in the Horn of Africa. Laas Geel's rock art is estimated to be approximately 5,500 to 4,500 years old.

landmarks.name: Arba'a Rukun Mosque
landmarks.writeup: One of the oldest mosques in Mogadishu, reflecting Islamic architecture and history.

wiki.extract: The Arba'a Rukun Mosque, also known as Arba Rucun, is a mosque in the Shangani medieval district of Mogadishu, Banaadir, Somalia.

landmarks.name: Mogadishu Cathedral
landmarks.writeup: A historic cathedral built during Italian colonial rule, symbolizing Somalia's diverse heritage.

wiki.extract: Mogadishu Cathedral is a ruined Catholic cathedral located in Mogadishu, Somalia. Between 1928 and 1991, it served as the seat of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Mogadiscio. Built in 1928 by Italian colonial authorities, much of the building was destroyed in 2008 by al-Shabaab. In 2013, the diocese announced plans to refurbish the building.

cultural_events.name: Eid al-Fitr
cultural_events.writeup: A major Islamic festival marking the end of Ramadan, celebrated with prayers, feasts, and community gatherings.

wiki.extract: Eid al-Fitr is the first of the two main festivals in Islam, the other being Eid al-Adha. The holiday falls on the first day of Shawwal, the tenth month of the Islamic calendar. One of the most important Islamic celebrations, Eid al-Fitr is celebrated by Muslims worldwide as it marks the end of the month-long, dawn-to-dusk fasting (sawm) during Ramadan. The holiday is known under various other names in different languages and countries around the world.

cultural_events.name: Somali Independence Day
cultural_events.writeup: Celebrated on July 1st, commemorating the unification of British Somaliland and Italian Somaliland in 1960.

wiki.extract: Independence Day is a national holiday occurring annually on July 1. The date celebrates the unification of the Trust Territory of Somalia and the State of Somaliland into the Somali Republic and the independence from the Italian Republic on July 1, 1960. A government was subsequently formed by Abdullahi Issa, Muhammad Haji Ibrahim Egal, and other members of the trusteeship and protectorate governments with Aden Abdullah Osman Daar as president. On July 20, 1961, through a referendum, the people of Somalia ratified a new constitution.

food_writeup: Somali cuisine features a blend of Middle Eastern and African flavors, with staple dishes like camel meat, rice, and flatbread, often spiced with cumin, coriander, and cardamom.
brief_history: Somalia has a rich history as a center of ancient trade and Islamic culture. It was colonized by Italy and Britain before gaining independence in 1960. The country has faced civil war and instability since the 1990s but continues efforts toward peace and development.
current_conflicts: Ongoing conflict with militant group Al-Shabaab, political instability, and regional disputes continue to affect Somalia's security and development.
